name: out-of-sight-out-of-mind
title: The Out-of-Sight Out-of-Mind ADHD mess type
description: The Out-of-Sight Out-of-Mind is the ADHD mess type where anything in a drawer stops existing. Why it is working memory, not mess, and the first card.

faq.q: Is ADHD object permanence a real thing?
faq.a: The phrase is colloquial. Adults with ADHD know an object still exists when it is hidden. What the research describes is a working-memory difference: things that are out of view drop out of the mental list faster. The lived experience is the same, so the fix is the same: keep what you use where you can see it.

faq.q: Will open storage just look like clutter?
faq.a: It can, if everything is out. The card is not permission to keep everything on the counter. It is a rule to give daily-use items one visible home each and put the rest away. Fewer objects in view, each with a spot, reads as calm and still stays findable.
